case.case_title: Wijeratne v. Vijitha Perera, Sub-Inspector of Police, Polonnaruwa and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No. 379/93, decided on 10 January 1994

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the police actions infringed the petitioner’s right to freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c) by obstructing a lawful trade union activity.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that the obstruction of the picketing campaign, a lawful activity of his trade union, infringed his freedom of association.
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents denied arrest and detention and claimed the petitioner was warned but could conduct peaceful picketing.
key_facts: Petitioner was secretary of a trade union branch involved in lawful collective action.
Police seized union posters and threatened the petitioner to prevent the protest.
The planned picketing was a legitimate activity of the union.
Police actions deterred the exercise of union rights.
No lawful authority justified police interference.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 14(1)(c) protects the right to freedom of association, including lawful trade union activities. The police interference unlawfully impaired this right.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the picketing was a legitimate union activity, the seizure of posters and threats to suppress the protest constituted an infringement of the petitioner’s freedom of association.
principles_established: Freedom of association includes the right to engage in lawful trade union activities.
State interference with lawful union activities without authority violates constitutional rights.
Protection of collective action is essential to democratic dissent.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s right to freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c) was infringed by the unlawful police actions.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation awarded and police directed to respect fundamental rights.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 14(1)(c) was central because the case involved suppression of lawful trade union activity, directly implicating freedom of association.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found that the obstruction of the lawful picketing campaign, a union activity, infringed the petitioner’s freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c).
